The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12d511db42d09b8c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 64. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every g as above, there is at most one family (hs)s>0 of probability densities with respect to Πg with the following properties: 1. hs ≥ 0, Πg[hs] = 1, and sups0≤s≤s1 ∥hs∥L∞(Πg) < ∞ whenever 0 < s0 < s1 < ∞; 2. hs+t = Sg t hs in L2(Πg) for s, t > 0, where Sg t = exp(−tc∗Hg); 3. there is a sequence sk ↓ 0 such that, for every i ≥ 1 and ε > 0, Πg h hsk 1{x2 i /M(x)>ε} i −→ 0. (6.3) Any such family satisfies hsΠg =⇒ δ0 on RN with its product topology, as s ↓ 0. (6.4) For almost every g such a family exists. It can be chosen measurably in g, as a family of L2(Πg) density classes, and with jointly measurable density representatives in (g, s, x). Every represented Gaussian limit in Proposition 5.1 is this family almost surely.
